chunks: And from him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Al-Husayn ibn Abdullah, who said:

Al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays and Ibn Abi Yafur accompanied each other on a journey. One of them ate the slaughtered meat of the Jews and Christians, while the other refused to eat it. They both gathered in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and informed him. He said: 'Which one of you two refused?' He said: 'I did.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Well done.'

key_terms.ذَبِيَةَ: Slaughtered meat (specifically that which is slaughtered)

ai.seo_question: Is the meat of Jews and Christians halal to eat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi illustrates the principle of *ikhtiyar* (choice) in fiqh, where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the permissibility of consuming the meat of the People of the Book while simultaneously praising the companion who abstained, indicating that refusal is also virtuous rather than erroneous. Historically, this reflects the practical legal flexibility granted to the early Shia community regarding dietary laws in mixed religious environments, emphasizing that both consumption and abstention are acceptable acts of worship. The Imam’s specific inquiry, 'Which of you abstained?', underscores the spiritual merit of caution (*wara'*) even in permissible matters.
